**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[France–Russia relations]]

[https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2022/mar/06/russia-ukraine-war-biden-and-zelenskiy-discuss-more-support-for-ukraine-as-visa-mastercard-pull-out-of-russia-live (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Ukraine]] suspends all exports of [[rye]], [[oat]], [[buckwheat]], [[millet]], [[sugar]], [[salt]], and most meat and meat products that are fit for human consumption, as the country expects poor harvests and food shortages. [https://zn.ua/ECONOMICS/ukraina-bolshe-ne-eksportiruet-mjaso-rozh-oves-hrechku-sakhar-proso-i-pishchevuju-sol.html (''Dzerkalo Tyzhnia'')]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]], [[2021–2022 global energy crisis]]
**The [[United States]] start talks with [[Venezuela]] about supplies of its oil, currently [[International sanctions during the Venezuelan crisis|under sanctions]], in an attempt to substitute the Russian crude. So far the talks yielded few results. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-venezuela-discuss-easing-sanctions-make-little-progress-sources-2022-03-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***The [[Chatham Islands]] near [[New Zealand]] reports its first case of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.1news.co.nz/2022/03/06/chatham-islands-record-first-cases-of-covid-19/ (TVNZ)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Enlargement of NATO]]
***[[Ukraine–NATO relations]]
****Ukrainian negotiator [[Davyd Arakhamia]] says that [[Ukraine]] is open to having non-[[NATO]] discussions in the future. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-open-discussing-non-nato-models-negotiator-tells-fox-news-2022-03-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[Russia–Turkey relations]]
***[[President of Turkey|Turkish president]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] calls for [[President of Russia|Russian president]] [[Vladimir Putin]] to declare a ceasefire between [[Russia]] and Ukraine. Putin tells Erdoğan that he is ready for dialogue in an effort to end the war but also warns that any attempt to draw out negotiations could fail. He also calls for Ukraine to cease fighting in order for the military campaign to end. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/03/06/erdogan-urges-urgent-general-ceasefire-in-putin-call-a76790 (''The Moscow Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/top-wrap-1-ukrainian-refugees-near-15-million-russian-assault-enters-11th-day-2022-03-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[Israel–Russia relations]]
***[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] says that [[Israel|his country]] will try to mediate a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia even if attempts are not successful. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/israels-bennett-returned-moscow-speaks-again-ukraines-zelenskiy-2022-03-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022 anti-war protests in Russia]]
***Around 4,000 [[Anti-war movement|anti-war]] demonstrators are arrested during protests in cities across Russia that are aimed at opposing the invasion. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-60640204 (BBC News)]
**[[Kazakhstan]] will allow anti-war protests in the country amidst fears that the country could be sanctioned. Protesters gather in [[Almaty]] to protest Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. [https://www.rferl.org/amp/kazakhstan-russia-ukraine-protest/31738906.html (Rferl)] [https://amp.france24.com/en/live-news/20220306-russia-ally-kazakhstan-permits-large-pro-ukraine-rally-amid-sanctions-fears (France 24)]
*[[Protests against responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**A convoy of truckers inspired by the [[Canada convoy protest|Canadian convoy protesters]] gather at the [[Capital Beltway]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] to call for all [[COVID-19]] restrictions and mandates to be lifted. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/06/us/trucker-convoy-protest-washington-dc-sunday/index.html (CNN)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Kwangmyŏngsŏng program]]
**[[North Korea]] says that it performed data transmission and other key tests to make a [[Reconnaissance satellite|reconnaissance spy satellite]]. This comes a day after the country [[2021–2022 North Korean missile tests|conducted]] a missile test. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/International/wireStory/north-korea-confirms-tests-spy-satellite-83277075 (ABC News)]
*[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**A Russian government directive is published ordering moving all government institutions and [[Internet service provider]]s servicing them to switch to Russian [[DNS]] servers and (whenever possible and applicable) to the [[.ru]] domain zone as well as substitute all foreign-hosted [[Javascript]] code with equivalent code hosted onshore by March 11. Russian authorities, however, do not plan to cut off from the global Internet network themselves. [https://www.theregister.com/2022/03/07/russia_tech_stimulus/ (''The Register'')] [https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/5249500 (''Kommersant'')]
